_**Assistant**_

To upgrade an Odoo module inside a running Docker container without restarting the container, you can use the Odoo CLI upgrade command. Here are the methods:

## Method 1: Using docker exec with Odoo CLI

```bash
# Upgrade a specific module
docker exec -it <container_name> odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d <database_name> -u <module_name> --stop-after-init

# Example for your setup (assuming container name is odoo-dev and module is om_hospital)
docker exec -it odoo-dev odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo -u om_hospital --stop-after-init
```

## Method 2: Using Odoo shell for live upgrade

```bash
# Access Odoo shell
docker exec -it odoo-dev odoo shell -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo

# Then in the shell, upgrade the module
env['ir.module.module'].search([('name', '=', 'om_hospital')]).button_immediate_upgrade()
```

## Method 3: Direct XML file modification and module reload

If you only modified XML files (views, data, etc.), you can:

```bash
# 1. Copy the modified files to the container (if needed)
docker cp ./custom-addons/om_hospital/views/patient_view.xml odoo-dev:/mnt/extra-addons/om_hospital/views/

# 2. Upgrade the module
docker exec -it odoo-dev odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo -u om_hospital --stop-after-init
```

## Method 4: Using the web interface (Developer mode)

1. Enable developer mode in Odoo web interface
2. Go to Apps menu
3. Remove "Apps" filter and search for your module
4. Click "Upgrade" button

## Quick one-liner for your setup:

```bash
docker exec -it odoo-dev odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo -u om_hospital --stop-after-init
```

This will upgrade the `om_hospital` module without restarting the container. The `--stop-after-init` flag ensures the upgrade process completes and then stops, leaving your main Odoo process running.

_**Assistant**_

Based on your docker-compose.yml, here's the updated one-liner and log checking commands:

## Quick one-liner for upgrading om_hospital module:

```bash
docker exec -it o15 odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo -u om_hospital --stop-after-init
```

## Check docker logs for the web service:

```bash
# Follow logs in real-time
docker logs -f o15

# Or check recent logs (last 50 lines)
docker logs --tail 50 o15

# Check logs with timestamps
docker logs -t o15
```

## Complete workflow for module upgrade with log monitoring:

```bash
# 1. Start monitoring logs in one terminal
docker logs -f o15

# 2. In another terminal, upgrade the module
docker exec -it o15 odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d odoo -u om_hospital --stop-after-init

# 3. Check if upgrade was successful in the logs
docker logs --tail 20 o15 | grep -i "om_hospital\|upgrade\|error"
```

The container name `o15` is used instead of `odoo-dev` as specified in your `docker-compose.yml` file. The logs will show you the upgrade process and any potential errors during the module update.
